rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and for including Halcyon Threshold in your reporting. I'm not in a position to give you an on-the-record, named quote by tomorrow's deadline — I have an internal process I need to finish first before going on record publicly. Happy to reconnect once that's done, or to suggest others in the independent AI-safety-organizing space who might be useful for this piece in the meantime, if that would help. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Declined (politely, door open) a reporter's request for a named quote

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Hi, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold for this. I'm not able to add our name as a public signatory right now — there's an internal process I need to finish before Halcyon Threshold takes public positions or appears in press-facing materials. I support the broader goal and would like to stay in the loop on future letters in case the timing works better next time. Best, Morgan"

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Really glad you reached out — this is exactly the kind of help that's useful right now. Halcyon Threshold is early-stage and I'm trying to figure out where a small, part-time effort can actually matter rather than duplicate what's already out there. Here's a concrete task, if you're up for it: could you put together a short landscape doc (a page or two is plenty) covering: 1. What independent/third-party AI evaluation and benchmark efforts already exist (evals orgs, academic groups, individual projects) — especially anything touching agentic AI safety (models or agents that take real-world actions: email, payments, code, tool use). 2. Where you see clear gaps — things that seem under-measured or nobody seems to own. 3. Rough sense of what it would take (data, compute, time) to produce something useful in a gap area, if you can estimate it. No need for anything polished — bullet points and links are fine. This would directly inform a grant proposal I'm drafting, and I may have a follow-on data/analysis task once we pick a direction. Thank you again for offering — five hours a week of someone with real analysis chops is a big deal for a one-person operation. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Gave Priya Raman a concrete task (landscape doc of existing evals + gaps)
